title: Burleson
name: Burleson
metaTitle: Burleson 1031 Exchange Investors | Fort Worth, TX
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Burleson investors trading I-35W corridor industrial and retail against older Old Town storefronts and service buildings.

sections.html: Burleson sits along the I-35W corridor south of Fort Worth, and its commercial base splits between highway-facing retail and light-industrial space drawn by that access, and a smaller historic downtown core known locally as Old Town that carries an entirely different tenant profile and building stock. An exchanger evaluating Burleson without separating these two profiles risks applying one submarket's pricing logic to the other's very different tenant base.

sections.heading: Highway Access Drives the Industrial and Retail Corridor
sections.html: Light-industrial and distribution buildings along I-35W in Burleson typically lease to regional operators who value proximity to the highway over proximity to downtown Fort Worth itself. Confirming actual loading, dock, and clear-height specifications against the lease and any recorded easement is a more reliable underwriting step than relying on a listing's general description of highway access. Confirming the tenant's actual trailer and truck-turning radius against the site plan, rather than the marketing brochure's stated acreage alone, is a useful check before assuming a specific use will fit the parcel as configured. A lease that references a shared access easement with a neighboring parcel should also be checked to confirm that easement is still recorded and unmodified, since older Burleson industrial parcels sometimes changed hands without updating that record.

sections.heading: Commercial Property Types an Exchanger Finds in Burleson
sections.html:
The stock here splits between two distinct submarkets, the highway corridor and the historic core:

  • light-industrial and distribution buildings along the I-35W corridor
  • grocery- or general-merchandise-anchored retail centers near the highway frontage
  • older storefronts in the Old Town historic core, leased to small local retailers and service businesses
  • self-storage and flex-space facilities serving the surrounding residential growth
  • a limited stock of medical and professional office buildings serving the local population

Retail along the highway frontage has generally kept pace with the corridor's residential growth, while Old Town's smaller storefronts depend more on local foot traffic than on any regional draw.

sections.heading: Identification Strategy Between Highway Industrial and Old Town Retail
sections.html: An exchanger exiting a highway-facing industrial building with a single regional tenant often benefits from the 200% rule, keeping Old Town retail or a DST interest available as a diversification option rather than a narrow list confined to similar single-tenant industrial product. A DST interest backed by diversified industrial or retail holdings can also serve as a lower-management alternative to taking on direct landlord responsibility for a single regional tenant.

sections.heading: Old Town's Older Building Stock Needs Its Own Diligence Path
sections.html: Storefronts in Burleson's historic Old Town core are often older buildings that may not carry the same documented capital-improvement history as newer highway-corridor construction. Confirming the roof, foundation, and mechanical system condition through an independent inspection, rather than relying on a seller's representation alone, is a necessary step before counting on the replacement property's near-term capital needs. Where a seller cannot produce records for a prior roof replacement or foundation repair, budgeting for that capital need directly, rather than assuming the building is in turnkey condition, is the more conservative approach.

sections.heading: Coordinating Closing Across Two Different Property Profiles
sections.html: A highway-corridor industrial building and an Old Town storefront can carry very different lender underwriting requirements, so the qualified intermediary and title company should confirm early which specific replacement property is moving toward closing. That keeps the lender's documentation request and the closing schedule matched to that property's actual profile rather than a generic Burleson description. Confirming financing terms early with a lender familiar with both property types, rather than one accustomed only to one or the other, also reduces the risk of a mismatched underwriting timeline.

faqs.q: How reliable is a listing's description of highway access for Burleson industrial property?
faqs.a: Actual loading, dock, and clear-height specifications should be confirmed against the lease and any recorded easement rather than relying on a general description of I-35W access in the listing.

faqs.q: How many properties should I identify exiting a single-tenant industrial building in Burleson?
faqs.a: More than three is common when the building leases to one regional tenant, since the 200% rule allows Old Town retail or a DST interest to stay on the list as a diversification option.

faqs.q: What should I check before buying an older storefront in Burleson's Old Town core?
faqs.a: An independent inspection of the roof, foundation, and mechanical systems is worth requesting directly, since older Old Town buildings may not carry the same documented capital-improvement history as newer highway-corridor construction.

faqs.q: Do lenders treat Old Town retail and highway-corridor industrial the same way?
faqs.a: No. Each typically carries different underwriting requirements, so confirming which specific replacement property is moving toward closing helps the lender's documentation request match that property's actual profile.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange Fort Worth confirm my Burleson property qualifies for exchange treatment?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates documentation and scheduling among the investor's advisors. Qualification determinations are made by the investor's CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary.

faqs.q: Does highway-corridor retail in Burleson depend on the same customer base as Old Town storefronts?
faqs.a: No. Highway frontage retail has generally tracked the corridor's residential growth, while Old Town's smaller storefronts depend more on local foot traffic than on a regional draw, so each should be evaluated against its own customer base.

faqs.q: Are shared access easements a common issue with older Burleson industrial parcels?
faqs.a: They can be. Some older parcels changed ownership over the years without formally updating a shared access or driveway easement, so confirming the recorded easement is current, rather than assumed from years of informal use, is worth the extra title review step.
